# Filter language


A filter is the `filters` object of an observer's source. It decides whether one call of the
observed function reaches one observer's target. The language is declarative JSON (`iii-filter` v1):
small, total, without side effects or regular expressions, so the same filter gives the same answer
wherever it runs:

- in the engine, for every call it routes: it holds the call's input, caller, and metadata, and
  takes its output or error from the answer of the worker that ran it. Engine-hosted functions and
  functions registered with `invocation` (HTTP-invoked) are among them;
- in the SDK of the worker that hosts the function, for the calls it makes to its own functions,
  which the engine never sees, and in `obs.matches(call)`.

The engine, the Rust SDK (`iii-filter` crate), and the Node, browser, Python, and Go evaluators all
run the same conformance vectors
([`sdk/fixtures/filters`](https://github.com/iii-hq/iii/tree/main/sdk/fixtures/filters)). For how
observers use filters, see [Observers](../using-iii/observers#filters).

<Note>
  `args` are for the function's worker and `filters` are for iii. A function's `args` (a schedule, a
  route, a table) go to the worker that hosts it, whose hooks decide what to set up and which
  observers each call is for. Filters decide which of those calls reach the target, and the worker
  never changes them.
</Note>

## The document

A filter reads one document per call, with five roots:

```jsonc
{
  "input": { "order_id": "o-1", "total": 750 }, // what the function was called with
  "output": { "status": "created" }, // present only on success
  "error": { "code": "TIMEOUT", "message": "..." }, // present only on failure
  "caller": {
    "worker_id": "3f1c...",
    "worker_name": "billing",
    "function_id": "billing::close-invoice", // absent for top-level calls
    "invocation_id": "c3f...",
    "parent": { "worker_name": "api", "function_id": "api::checkout", "invocation_id": "77..." },
  },
  "metadata": { "tenant": "acme" }, // the invocation's metadata sidecar
}
```

- A filter may reference any root, whatever the observer captures. `capture` only decides what is
  shipped to the target.
- `on` (`success`, `error`, `complete`) is checked before the filter.
- `output` is the handler's return value, which is what observers observe. An event source's handler
  returns the event it is called with, so its `input` and `output` are the same value.

## Syntax

```text
Filters   := { Clause, ... }                     // all clauses must match; {} matches everything
Clause    := "<path>": { "$op": operand, ... }   // all operators on that path must match
           | "$and": [Filters, ...]
           | "$or":  [Filters, ...]
           | "$not": Filters
Path      := root ("." segment)*                 // root: input | output | error | caller | metadata
segment   := key | index                         // index: "0" or a decimal without a leading zero
```

A path clause always takes an **operator object**. There is no literal shorthand:
`{ "input.op": "insert" }` is `INVALID_FILTER`; write `{ "input.op": { "$eq": "insert" } }`.

- A filter is a JSON object. Anything else, `null` included, is `INVALID_FILTER`. An absent
  `filters` matches every call.
- A filter object holds paths, `$and`, `$or`, and `$not`. Any other `$` key is `INVALID_FILTER`,
  value operators included (`{ "$eq": 1 }` needs a path).
- `$and` and `$or` take a non-empty array of filters (`[]` is `INVALID_FILTER`). `$not` takes one
  filter. `{}` is allowed there (`{ "$not": {} }` matches nothing) and as a member of `$and` or
  `$or` (it matches everything).
- An operator object is non-empty and holds only value operators. An empty `{}`, a key without `$`,
  an unknown operator, or `$and` / `$or` / `$not` inside it is `INVALID_FILTER`.

### Paths

- A path splits on unescaped dots. `\.` is a literal dot and `\\` a literal backslash; any other
  backslash sequence and a trailing backslash are `INVALID_FILTER`. In a JSON string the backslash
  itself is escaped: `"input.headers.x\\.tenant"`.
- An empty path or an empty segment (`input.`, `.input`, `input..a`) is `INVALID_FILTER`.
- The first segment is the root: `input`, `output`, `error`, `caller`, or `metadata`
  (case-sensitive). A path may be the root alone: `"error": { "$exists": true }`.
- An index segment (`0`, `1`, `12`) selects an array element. `01` and `-1` are keys, never indexes.
  On an object, a numeric segment is a key.
- `@` is a root only inside `$any`, where every path starts at it. After the root, `@` is an
  ordinary key.

## Operators

| Operator                  | Operand                   | Matches when                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `$eq`                     | any JSON                  | the value is deep equal to the operand                                |
| `$ne`                     | any JSON                  | the value is not deep equal to the operand, **or the path is absent** |
| `$in`                     | array (at most 256 items) | the value is deep equal to some item                                  |
| `$nin`                    | array (at most 256 items) | the value is deep equal to no item, **or the path is absent**         |
| `$gt` `$gte` `$lt` `$lte` | number or string          | the value has the operand's JSON type and compares accordingly        |
| `$exists`                 | boolean                   | the path's presence equals the operand                                |
| `$prefix`                 | string                    | the value is a string that starts with the operand                    |
| `$any`                    | operator object or filter | the value is an array and at least one element matches                |

The operators of one operator object must all match:
`{ "input.total": { "$gte": 100, "$lt": 500 } }` is a range.

### `$any`

There is no implicit fan-out over arrays: `input.items.sku` on an array of items is absent. Use
`$any`:

- **Scalar elements:** pass an operator object. `{ "input.tags": { "$any": { "$eq": "vip" } } }`
- **Object elements:** pass a filter whose paths start at `@`, the current element.
  `{ "input.items": { "$any": { "@.sku": { "$eq": "A-1" }, "@.qty": { "$gte": 10 } } } }`

`{ "$any": {} }` matches any non-empty array. A nested `$any` binds `@` to its own element. An empty
array, a value that is not an array, and an absent path do not match. Mixing operators and paths in
one `$any` object is `INVALID_FILTER`.

## Matching rules

- **Absent paths.** A path yields a value or is absent: stepping into a scalar, a missing key, or an
  out-of-range index yields absent. Only `$ne`, `$nin`, and `$exists: false` match an absent path;
  every other operator is false. `$not` negates its whole filter, so it matches when the inner path
  is absent.
- **`null` is a value.** `{ "$exists": true }` matches `null`, and `{ "$eq": null }` matches only
  `null`, never an absent path.
- **Own keys only.** `constructor`, `toString`, and `__proto__` are ordinary keys that resolve only
  when the document holds them.
- **Equality** is JSON deep equality. Object key order is ignored; array order is not. There is no
  coercion between types: `0`, `false`, `null`, `""`, and `"0"` all differ. Strings are equal when
  their code points are (no Unicode normalization).
- **Numbers** compare as IEEE-754 doubles: `1` equals `1.0`, and `-0` equals `0`. A payload integer
  above 2^53 is rounded to the nearest double first. Numeric literals in a filter must be within
  ±2^53 (9007199254740992), floats included (`1e16` is `INVALID_FILTER`).
- **Ordering** applies within one type only. Numbers compare numerically; strings compare by Unicode
  code point (UTF-8 byte order, not JavaScript's UTF-16 order). Any other pairing (mixed types,
  `null`, booleans, arrays, objects, absent) is false for all four operators.
- **`$in: []`** matches nothing; **`$nin: []`** matches everything, absent included. An array value
  is compared with each item as a whole.
- **`$prefix: ""`** matches every string.
- **Host values.** SDKs evaluate as if on the JSON encoding of the document: `undefined` is absent,
  a `Date` is its ISO string, and a `BigInt` or `Decimal` compares through its JSON number.
- **Totality.** A filter that was valid at creation answers true or false for every document. It
  never fails.

## Many observers

The engine matches a call against all of a function's observers through an index of their filters'
equality conditions. It files each observer under one `$eq` (or `$in`) condition of its top-level
`$and` whose operand is a scalar (a number, a string, a boolean, or `null`), by path and value, and
keeps the observers without one in a list. A call costs one lookup per indexed path, plus a full
evaluation of the filters it finds there and of those in the list: with 4,000 observers that each
filter on their own `input.tenant`, a call evaluates one filter. The index uses the equality rules
above (`1` and `1.0` are one value), so its matches are exactly the observers whose filters match.

A filter costs a call nothing when the call does not meet the condition the index files it under.
The index files each filter under one condition only, preferring an `$eq` to an `$in` and the value
the fewest other observers are filed under, so a filter with several equality conditions is
evaluated on every call that meets the one it is filed under, whatever its other conditions say. A
filter without one (its conditions are ranges, `$ne`, `$nin`, `$exists`, `$prefix`, conditions
inside `$or`, `$not`, or `$any`, or an `$eq` of an array or an object) is evaluated on every call.

## Validation

The engine validates every filter when an observer is created and answers `INVALID_FILTER` or
`INVALID_FILTER_PATH` in the observer's `error` state.

### Limits

| Limit          | Value      | What counts                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Depth          | 8          | The top-level filter is depth 1. Each `$or` member, `$not` operand, and `$any` operand is one level deeper than the object holding it. `$and` members stay at the same depth. |
| Nodes          | 64         | Each value operator (`$eq` ... `$any`) and each `$or` / `$not` counts 1. Paths and `$and` are free.                                                                           |
| `$in` / `$nin` | 256 items  | Per array.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Path segments  | 16         | Segments after the root (also after `@`).                                                                                                                                     |
| Literal depth  | 32         | Arrays and objects nested in one `$eq` / `$ne` operand or one `$in` / `$nin` item. A scalar is 0, `[1]` is 1, `{"a": [1]}` is 2.                                              |
| JSON depth     | 120        | Arrays and objects nested in the whole filter value, `$and` wrappers and literals included.                                                                                   |
| Encoded size   | 8192 bytes | UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON of the filter **as written**.                                                                                                                 |

Every limit fails with `INVALID_FILTER`. Documents have no limits.

### Schema checks

When the observed function registered a `request_format` (for `input.*` paths) or a
`response_format` (for `output.*` paths), the engine checks each path against the schema's
`properties` and `items`:

- A property that a closed schema (`additionalProperties: false`) does not declare is
  `INVALID_FILTER_PATH`, so a typo such as `input.tabel` fails at creation instead of matching
  nothing.
- Under an open schema, the same path is accepted with a warning in the observer's result. So is a
  construct the check cannot follow: a remote `$ref`, `anyOf` / `oneOf` / `allOf` with several
  branches, `patternProperties`, or `if`. Local `$ref`s and nullable wrappers are followed.
- A path that reaches a `false` schema is `INVALID_FILTER_PATH`.
- `@` paths inside `$any` are checked against the array's `items`.
- When the function is not registered yet, the checks run when it registers.

Schema checks run in the engine only. `args` are validated separately, against the observed
function's `args_format` (`INVALID_ARGS`), and filters cannot reference them.

## Normal form

The engine normalizes every filter before it stores it or pushes it to the worker that hosts the
function (`engine::observers::list` shows the normal form too):

- Every filter, nested ones included, becomes `{}` or `{ "$and": [ ... ] }` with one clause per
  object.
- Explicit `$and`s are flattened into the filter that holds them.
- Clauses are sorted by key in byte order (`$not` and `$or` before paths), then by the compact JSON
  of their operand, and exact duplicates are dropped.
- Operator object keys are sorted. Operands, `$in` / `$nin` items, paths, and the order of `$or`
  members are kept as written. `$ne` and `$nin` are not rewritten.

```jsonc
// as written
{ "input.b": { "$lt": 5 }, "input.a": { "$eq": 1 } }

// normal form
{ "$and": [ { "input.a": { "$eq": 1 } }, { "input.b": { "$lt": 5 } } ] }
```

Normalizing is idempotent and matches exactly the documents its source matches. It never increases
the depth, node, item, segment, or literal limits; the encoded size can grow, so workers compile the
normal form they receive without the size limit.

## Examples

```jsonc
// updates that touched more than 100 rows
{ "input.op": { "$eq": "update" }, "input.affected_rows": { "$gt": 100 } }

// writes made on behalf of anyone except the search indexer (stops echo loops)
{ "caller.parent.worker_name": { "$ne": "search-indexer" } }

// failed charges above 500, or any failure with a timeout code
{ "$or": [
    { "input.amount": { "$gt": 500 }, "error": { "$exists": true } },
    { "error.code": { "$eq": "TIMEOUT" } } ] }

// an order with at least one line item of 10 or more units of SKU A-1
{ "input.items": { "$any": { "@.sku": { "$eq": "A-1" }, "@.qty": { "$gte": 10 } } } }

// requests for one tenant, from a header whose name contains a dot
{ "input.headers.x\\.tenant": { "$eq": "acme" } }

// everything except health checks
{ "$not": { "input.path": { "$prefix": "/health" } } }
```

## From iii lang predicates

A filter maps one to one to a predicate of the iii language, which is why the language accepts
explicit operators only:

| iii lang predicate         | `filters`                             |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `'p' == v`                 | `{ "p": { "$eq": v } }`               |
| `'p' != v`                 | `{ "p": { "$ne": v } }`               |
| `'p' < v`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`          |
| `'p' in [a, b]`, `not in`  | `$in`, `$nin`                         |
| `a && b`                   | two clauses (implicit AND), or `$and` |
| `a \|\| b`                 | `$or`                                 |
| `!a`                       | `$not`                                |

`$exists`, `$prefix`, and `$any` map to functions of the predicate language.

## Evaluate a filter in code

A worker evaluates an observer's filters, with its `on`, through `obs.matches(call)` (`Matches` in
Go). An `onObserverDeliver` hook that runs a target itself with `iii.call({ observer, payload })`
checks the call this way first, for example to answer a request differently when the filters reject
it. The Python, Rust, and Go SDKs also expose the evaluator itself, which is handy in tests:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    from iii.filter import compile_filter

    f = compile_filter({"input.amount": {"$gte": 500}})
    f.matches({"input": {"amount": 750}})  # True
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::Filter;
    use serde_json::json;

    let filter = Filter::parse(&json!({ "input.amount": { "$gte": 500 } }))?;
    assert!(filter.matches_value(&json!({ "input": { "amount": 750 } })));
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    import "github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii/filter"

    f, err := filter.Compile(map[string]any{"input.amount": map[string]any{"$gte": 500}})
    if err != nil {
        return err // a *filter.Error with code INVALID_FILTER
    }
    f.Matches(filter.Map{"input": map[string]any{"amount": 750}}) // true
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>
